facts.fact: Ammu's market cover is 'Valli', a coast-side pepper trader's girl who came up with the last cart before the passes close.
facts.why: needed because Ammu must be disguised and Neela must name her in front of Muthu.

facts.fact: Parukutty is a soldier's widow in the lower village with a six-year-old daughter and a nine-year-old son; her husband Raman, a spearman, died on Devan's patrol in spring. She owes the salt factor six and a half measures plus a tally fee.
facts.why: needed because the outline requires a widow's salt debt that Devan clears.

facts.fact: Muthu goes down to the lower market with the garrison's purse on market days, and tells Neela that Devan hates market day.
facts.why: needed to explain why Muthu is at the next stall without coincidence.

facts.fact: Chathu's message to Neela: the writ is on the road; after it lands every day counts double; if the account is open when the pass closes he will force resin on her and read her page aloud at dusk.
facts.why: carries the outline's guild message in Chathu's debts-and-balances voice.

facts.fact: Neela counts thirty-four nights left on the morning of chapter 7.
The tune Ammu hums is a fishing song with the refrain 'Pull and pull, the tide is coming in'.
facts.why: gives the bible's invented fishing song a concrete refrain.
